description: The key set behind db/user_settings.json. Same kind of value as const.json holds, but changeable at runtime instead of at release. The tables are generic; this file is what makes a row typed, bounded and readable by both implementations.
valueEncoding: Every value in the database is text, in the same form contracts/ uses everywhere: a decimal string for every numeric type, 'true' or 'false' for bool, UTC milliseconds for an instant. 'default' below carries that same text form, so a default and a stored value are never encoded differently.

hide_amount_gdd.description: The member hides their own GDD balance in the header. About their own view only — nobody else's response depends on it.

hide_amount_gdt.description: The member hides their own GDT balance in the header. About their own view only — nobody else's response depends on it.

main_creation_group.description: The member's main creation group: what the group field is pre-filled with when they submit a contribution, and what a moderator sets for them when seeding a whole organisation at once. NULL means they have none.
main_creation_group.note: The value is a creation_groups.id as a decimal string, not the tag. An admin may rename a tag through creationGroup.edit, and a preference that silently stops matching after a rename is the failure this encoding removes. An id that resolves to no row is read as unset and logged at warn — the same soft failure a deleted group produces.

notes: A key is an identifier and follows the rule the rest of contracts/ follows: rename nothing, reuse nothing. To retire one, mark it deprecated and leave it here — a database written by an older release still holds rows under the old name.
'default' is what an implementation returns when no row exists, and every implementation returns exactly this. It is not a suggestion and it is not re-derived from an environment variable.

A default of null is only legal together with nullable: true. Everywhere else null in the database is a value that failed to parse, and the reading implementation falls back to this default and logs an error — see db/settings.json.
min, max and the string bounds are validation for the admin frontend and for both implementations, which must reject the same value. A bound is not decoration.

main_creation_group replaces the user_creation_groups table, which gradido2 does not have. Legacy modelled it as an ordered many-to-many with a sort_order, but only ../gradido/admin ever wrote it, always with exactly one tag or none (ChangeUserRoleFormular.vue, saveUserMainTag), every save replaced the whole list in one transaction (backend/src/graphql/resolver/util/userCreationGroups.ts), and the only reader takes personal[0] (util/suggestCreationGroup.ts). A table whose logic can never hold more than one row is a setting.

The migration takes the row with the lowest sort_order, ties broken by the lowest id — legacy's own order — and writes its creation_group_id. A member with more than one row is a state legacy's write path cannot produce; if one exists anyway, the extra rows are dropped and logged at warn rather than being silently picked between.
